title: Minimalist reassurance digest and self-serve recovery paths (draft)
body:
Draft purpose: a short, easy-to-read status and follow-up note customers can digest quickly and act on if they want. This is intentionally concise — a one-page reassurance + 3 self-serve choices. Use for status page updates, email templates, and partner-side ops.

TL;DR
- What happened: A routing cascade in the EU inference pool caused elevated latency and intermittent failed responses for a subset of streaming sessions between 2026-04-14 02:12 UTC and 2026-04-14 03:40 UTC.
- Scope: ~1.7% of hosted API requests during window; primarily short-chat streaming sessions using model-family:redwood-chat-2x in eu-west-1. No customer data lost.
- Current status: Mitigations applied; traffic fully routed to warmed fallback capacity as of 03:40 UTC. We are verifying integrity of queued requests and replays.

Impact at a glance (customer-facing matrix)
- Symptom: high streaming latency / truncated streams
- Affected: hosted API customers with streaming enabled in eu-west-1
- Severity: degraded experience (not data corruption)
- Recommended immediate action: none required — we applied an automated fallback. If you observed persistent missing responses, review "Self-serve verification" below.

Root cause (short-form, non-technical summary)
- Initial trigger: a rare race between autoscaler drain + routing refresh that momentarily over-directed active streams to a node set undergoing cache eviction.
- Why customer-visible: that node drop introduced partial token-generation stalls for streaming sessions; the routing policy did not fall back immediately to a warmed pool.
- Ongoing: we have a primary RCA being prepared (engineering after-action). This note is to help customers reconcile impact and next steps.

Immediate mitigation we took
- Automated routing fallback invoked to route new sessions to warmed spare capacity (applied ~02:20 UTC).
- Throttled (soft) new warm-up requests to limit eviction noise while we stabilized pools.
- Manual reconciliation job run to reprocess queued inference work where applicable (started 02:45 UTC, completed 03:35 UTC for most tenants).

Current verification state (what customers should know)
- Metrics: error-rate and 95th latency returned to baseline by 03:40 UTC.
- Integrity: we have no indicators of model output corruption.
- Replay backlog: <0.05% of requests flagged for optional reprocessing. We will surface affected request ids to tenants who opt in.

Self-serve verification steps (short; copy into support emails)
1) Check status page: https://status.redwood.ai — incident stub: "EU streaming latency (2026-04-14)"
2) For API customers: run a quick health call (non-streaming) to confirm baseline routing: curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $API_KEY" https://api.redwood.ai/v1/health
3) To detect truncated streaming responses: confirm last_event == "done" in your stream event payloads for sessions during 02:10–03:50 UTC. If you see sessions ending early, collect a single example (request_id + timestamps) and attach to support case.
4) If you want us to reprocess flagged requests: reply with consent and tenant id; we will re-run replay job and provide an evidence bundle.

Customer options (3 simple paths)
- Do nothing (recommended if you did not see issues): we already applied fallbacks and monitoring; no action required.
- Opt-in replay (recommended if you saw missing content): we will reprocess requests flagged during the window and deliver a reconciliation report + evidence bundle. This requires explicit tenant consent.
- Manual verification (advanced): if you need granular proof, we will provide request-level logs and a compact evidence package (signed checksums + timestamps) under an agreed NDA for enterprise tenants.

Status page snippets (short variants you can drop into updates)
- Detection update (first broadcast): "We detected elevated latency and intermittent streaming failures in eu-west-1 impacting a small subset of hosted API customers. Mitigation is in progress. We will post an update within 30 minutes."
- Recovery update (when routing fallback active): "Traffic has been rerouted to warmed capacity. Latency and errors are returning to normal. If you continue to see issues, open a support ticket and include an example request_id."
- Closure/assurance (post-verification): "Service restored and monitoring shows stable behavior. We found no evidence of data loss. An engineering after-action summary will be published to affected customers in the next 72 hours."

Suggested short email to affected customers
Subject: Quick update — EU streaming latency event (Apr 14)
Body: Hi <Customer>,
We detected a short disruption affecting streaming responses in eu-west-1 on Apr 14 between 02:12–03:40 UTC. We routed traffic to fallback capacity and verified the service returned to baseline. If you saw truncated or missing responses and would like us to reprocess flagged requests, reply with the tenant id and we will initiate an opt-in replay and send a reconciliation report. Our engineering team is preparing a short after-action for you. Apologies for the disruption — please contact <support@redwood.ai> and include request_id examples if available.

FAQ (customer-friendly)
Q: Was any customer data exposed or lost?
A: No evidence of data loss or exposure. This was a routing/latency event that affected response delivery for some streaming sessions.

Q: Will I be charged for reprocessed requests?
A: Replays performed by Redwood for remediation will be provided as a one-time operational courtesy. We will not bill reprocessed events.

Q: Will this happen again?
A: We have applied a configuration patch to reduce the race window and are testing a longer-term fix to the autoscaler/routing handshake. We will share timelines in the after-action.

Operator/checklist notes (internal)
- Post short status page update (initial) — @oncall (done)
- Open customer list and tag affected tenants — CS triage (in progress)
- Prepare opt-in replay opt sheet and evidence kit template — Eng + CS (todo)
- Draft after-action for customers including timeline + root cause (eng lead) — target 72h

Open questions for engineering team (for RCA)
- Confirm exact autoscaler event sequence and whether a single node reported repeated evictions.
- Confirm whether cache eviction threshold needs a conservative buffer for streaming sessions.
- Validate that fallback routing window is reduced to <30s in the next config patch.

Contact & escalation
- CS owner: Avery Chen (avery.chen@redwood.ai)
- Engineering lead: Jordan Lee (jordan.lee@redwood.ai) — follow-up RCA
- Live support: support@redwood.ai (include tenant id + request_id examples)

Notes to self (tone / publishing guidance)
- Keep public wording non-technical and reassuring. Use the status page snippets above for sequential updates.
- For enterprise customers with legal/regulatory constraints, offer the full evidence package and a direct briefing.
- This draft should be copy-edited and approved by legal for wording about "no data loss" before final customer closure note is sent.

End of draft.

Revision history:
- 2026-04-14 initial draft by Avery Chen
- 2026-04-16 added verification steps and snippets (Priya Kapoor)
- 2026-04-20 updated scope numbers and replay policy (Jordan Lee)
